analysis.title: Goldman's Macro Clients Are Rattled By The Speed Of The Bond Rout...
key_insights: Goldman macro clients are more concerned with the pace of the rate rise than the level. The roughly 68bp jump since end of August is the issue, and the same move over six months would have been received differently.
Oil and rates have stopped trading as one asset. Clients find the breakup unsettling, and nobody claims to be able to handicap de-escalation in the Gulf.

The 10Y was at 4.77% on Sep 3, traded around 5.32% on Thursday, and closed the week at 5.25% with the 2Y at 4.80%. The 30Y auction priced at 5.618%, the highest since August 2000, and the 10Y auction a day earlier priced at 5.30%, the highest since 2000.
Rikin Shah's Macro Roadmap calls the past month's move in the 10Y a two standard deviation event and argues against chasing it near term while the supply/demand imbalance persists.

MarketStrats: 2Y yields are up 64bp since Aug 4 and 149bp since late February. 3-month implied vol on 10Y USD swaps is up 28bp, a 2.3 standard deviation move that puts it at the 100th percentile of the past year.

April Li: the latest 20bp leg is a bear steepener, where the earlier move was a bear flattener. With 100bp of hikes priced, the front end has hit its limit and selling has moved out the curve, where term premium builds on fiscal math, supply, inflation uncertainty and fewer marginal buyers.
Li argues a yield level alone will not bring buyers back, even at 10Y 5.5% or 30Y 6%, while volatility is this high. The catalyst will come from volatility and news flow.
The Treasury's latest buyback drew $46 billion of offers against an average of about $10 billion in earlier operations, which Li reads as investors dumping off-the-run risk.

Of the 108bp selloff in 10Y yields that Shah tracks, 98bp is real rates. 30Y real yields are at 3.33%, near the top of the post-2010 range, so the market is repricing the cost of capital rather than an inflation scare.
Goldman rates strategists (William Marshall) say recent credit spread pressure shows weaker ability to absorb a high-vol selloff without tighter financial conditions, most visibly in Europe.

Treasurys have become asymmetric in their sensitivity to oil (April Li): they lost most of their positive beta when crude falls and kept a meaningful negative beta when it rises. Oil finished the week about $2.50 higher while the 10Y finished roughly flat.

Mark Wilson (London) argues longer-dated yields remain tightly correlated with 12-month forward crude, and stable energy prices would relieve the bond selloff and let stocks rally into year-end. Goldman's commodity team estimates a $22/bbl risk premium in spot Brent, the second highest monthly reading on record.
YTD the S&P is up about 14% and the S&P excluding AI (SPXXAI) is up about 7%. The gap widened to a record 10 points over five weeks before narrowing this week.

Miller thinks ex-AI already prices the rates-and-oil worry and would add non-AI exposure through consumer experiences, health care and SPXXAI upside (November 103% calls cost 0.75%). Health care correlation to AI, oil and the 10Y is close to zero. Clients see the midterms as a clearing event for AI power stocks.
Jack Singer: since 1974 the median S&P return is -3.5% in the month before a midterm and +6.5% in the four months after.

Of 21 systematic strategies in Miller's table, 10 sell volatility or harvest skew and 5 are dispersion. The top five by Sharpe are all vol-selling: daily equity skew harvesting 4.34, copper vol carry 3.55 (+30.9% YTD), weekly S&P variance carry 3.15, weekly WTI vol carry 2.69, VIX vol carry 2.68.

1-month S&P realized vol stayed below 13% over the past year while the VIX averaged 18. In September skew strategies added 93bp to 114bp, VIX carry made 201bp, and long-vol AI and Mag 7 strategies lost 125bp and 150bp.

Asset managers hold the largest net short in VIX futures on record, beyond July 2024, and vol-of-vol is near August lows. Goldman's Vol Views says this leaves the complex offside and exposed to a squeeze.
Dealers hold estimates of record long gamma, and assets in the five largest S&P overwriting ETFs reached a record above $65 billion at the start of October.
The VIX closed at 14.84 on Friday. Nasdaq November fixed-strike vol fell almost a full point, and a large seller of vol-of-vol in October VIX calls was seen.

Rate vol is at the top of its one-year range while equity vol is at the bottom. Continued risk reduction by short-vol accounts keeps rate vol elevated, and Simon Freycenet says higher rate vol has deepened the selloff by squeezing carry trades.
Zerohedge's view: the clients' fear of speed and the scoreboard of vol-selling returns are the same fact, since a market paid to assume small moves is least able to handle a large one.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil stabilizes, CPI behaves, earnings deliver and the short-vol trade collects another quarter. Goldman rates strategists see tactical value in fading the 10Y's underperformance, and the ex-AI market has already taken its punishment.
tension_points.bear_case: Record short VIX positioning, record dealer gamma and rate vol at a one-year high mean a single fast move in the wrong asset could trigger a squeeze, and unwinding of short-vol strategies feeds higher vol.
tension_points.what_invalidates: One fast day in the wrong asset, or a VIX squeeze as the record net short unwinds.

tension_points.bull_case: Mark Wilson: longer-dated yields remain tightly correlated with 12-month forward crude, so stable energy prices would relieve the bond selloff and let stocks rally into year-end.
tension_points.bear_case: Miller and April Li: Treasurys have lost most of their positive beta to falling crude but keep negative beta to rising crude, so de-escalation no longer rescues bonds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Falling crude producing a sustained fall in yields would restore the old link.
